text:
incident-bot: [PAGING] Streaming service: unusual quiet-spike in socket write path detected in eu-west-1. Auto-paging to #incidents. Incident token INC-20260315-QXJ.

jordan: seeing it — p95 jumped ~250ms -> ~2.0s at 23:04 UTC, p99 ~5.2s. Not a full outage, more stalls/long tails on streaming SSE/Ws.
maya: confirmed. traces show a cluster of connections with repeated zero-length writes then long pauses. client-side ack counters not moving.
sam: is this proxy-layer or origin runtime? initial grep looks like proxy write timeouts to streaming backends increased.
maya: metric snippets: 

```
// metrics snapshot 2026-03-15T23:04:10Z
streaming.p95_eu-west-1 = 2050ms
streaming.p99_eu-west-1 = 5200ms
proxy.write_timeouts_eu-west-1 = +120 (5m)
backend.kv_cache_hit_ratio = 0.86
connection.write_bytes_last_10s = 0 (for ~1200 sessions)
```

jordan: got a small log snippet from proxy 10.2.18.7: 

```
[23:04:12Z] warn: socket_write_timeout expired after 90s for session=abcd1234 client=acct-42 route=/v1/live stream=true
[23:04:12Z] info: queuing fallback to non-stream for session=abcd1234
```

oncall: copying runbook actions: 1) assess blast radius 2) scale proxy pool 3) force-degrade to non-streaming for heavy sessions 4) check keepalive/ALB timeouts.

customer-ops: three customers flagged via alerts: acme-inc (dedicated), betaapp (hosted), glue-ai (hosted). acme reported one-third of live requests stalling for >5s.

jordan: quick triage — looks like a subset of proxy workers entered a backpressure loop when many clients stopped reading (slow consumers). Downstream write buffer filled and proxy stopped sending chunks to other sessions due to head-of-line.
maya: we see elevated RTOs between proxy->runtime on the same pool around 23:03:50, packets retransmitted. Could be kernel-level socket congestion on those hosts.
sam: rolling deploy? any recent proxy changes in eu-west? deploy-bot: deploy triggered by ci-pipeline at 22:58 UTC to proxy-image v2.14.3 in eu-west-1 (3 workers).

jordan: ok, mitigation plan: 
- immediate: scale proxy pool +2 nodes in eu-west-1 (autoscale not catching fast enough)
- short: enable fast-fail for slow consumer sessions (conn-slow-threshold=30s) -> drop/convert to non-stream
- medium: rollback proxy image v2.14.3 on affected ASG if metrics don't improve in 10m
- longer: improve socket keepalive/epoll params and add per-connection write-window enforcement

maya: enacting scale now: `infractl scale asg proxy-eu-west1 +2` (kicking off).

oncall: doing live handoff to night oncall @oncall — please monitor p95/p99 and eviction counts. I'll stay on for a hot handover.

customer-ops: notified acme support@acme-inc with status note and mitigation steps, flagged high-impact, SLA watch.

sam: temporary knob to enable: `proxy.enable_stream_fastfail=true` on service config. I'm going to flip it for eu-west canary group.
maya: flipped canary to true on 3/6 proxies; watching. If we see client-side errors increase, we will convert to degrade route with `?stream=false` fallback.

[23:12:00Z] maya: after scale + canary flip: proxy.write_timeouts dropping (-75 over last 2m), p95 -> 420ms, p99 -> 1.4s. Some sessions got converted to non-stream and saw normal completion.
jordan: good signal. still seeing a small tail cluster ~0.5% sessions with repeated zero-byte writes. pulling tcpdump on 10.2.18.7 for those session ids.

oncall: handover: leaving notes for next shift — suspected regression in proxy v2.14.3 interacting with slow consumer connection handling. Follow-ups: kernel tuning, per-connection writeback, add telemetry for write-buffer-occupancy, consider rollback if reoccurs.

customer-ops: acme contact acknowledged mitigation, will keep SLA watch.

sam: creating incident ticket INC-20260315-QXJ intracker with root cause hypothesis and mitigation timeline. adding runbook links and dashboards: https://monitoring.redwood.ai/d/streaming/eu-west-1?from=now-30m

jordan: next steps: 1) continue to observe for 30m, 2) collect tcpdumps + strace for affected proxy workers, 3) schedule rollback if metrics worsen.

oncall: thanks team. I'll update #status and send an internal summary in 30m. :thumbsup:
